questions.learningObjective: Find the specific ask in a letter to an official

stimulus.body: Translator letter to the ministry describes delays and asks for an extension. requesting an extension is a specific ask, even alongside delay description. A marginal reminder adds: look for a concrete request. Four statements are offered, and only one follows from the note.

questions.stem: The passage invites “Find the specific ask in a letter to an official / Look for a concrete request. / A letter to an official: the specific ask”. Which option is the evidence-backed one?

options.text: There is no specific ask, because only delays are described.
options.misconception: selects "There is no specific ask, because only delays are…" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition

options.text: The letter refuses an ask, because it describes delays.
The specific ask is an extension, because it requests one.
The letter defers an ask, because it waits for a reply.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: requesting an extension is a specific ask, even alongside delay description. On that basis "The specific ask is an extension, because it requests one" is the supported choice. Option A ("There is no specific ask, because only delays are described") fails because it selects "There is no specific ask, because only delays are…" where a letter to an official: the specific ask requires a different condition; Option B ("The letter refuses an ask, because it describes delays") fails because it reads description as decline; Option D ("The letter defers an ask, because it waits for a reply") fails because it confuses courtesy with postponing.
